Designs

Final drive for the electric Formula Manipal car: a dual chain drive from the motor to the differential, designed in Fusion 360 and built in-house with CNC parts.

Dual chain drive concept

Fusion 360, ChassisSim

Problem
Single-motor EMRAX 208 MV (140 Nm peak) needed a final drive ratio of about 5.8 that packages inside the chassis.
My role
Transmission lead: concept, CAD, analysis, vendor drawings and testing.
Process
Weighted-average ratio from lap-time sims gave 5.843. Chosen 5.818 with two chain stages (22:11 and 32:11).
Dual chain drive cut rotating inertia by 54.4% (+1.36 kg) and avoided a 256 mm longer wheelbase.

Motorshaft and intermediate shaft assemblies

Fusion 360, SolidWorks, GD&T

Motorshaft
Three-piece shaft with M6 bolts, safety wiring, press-fit bearing and circlips. Mount in Al 7075, anodised.
Intermediate shaft
Eccentric discs in the mounts tension both chains by changing the centre distance. Shaft is single-piece EN19.
Positioning
Shaft placed from wrap-angle and teeth-in-contact calculations so the differential sits at chassis centre.
Shortest shaft that keeps sprocket clearance, with adjustable tensioning on both chains.

Differential and halfshafts

Fusion 360, hand calculations

Differential
Drexler 1.5-way limited slip differential, centred in the chassis so both halfshafts are equal length and torque steer is avoided.
Stubs
Aluminium 7075 stubs failed at launch, so they were redesigned in hardened EN24 steel.
Halfshafts
EN24, 20 mm outer and 15 mm inner diameter. Twist 14.9 deg vs 27.1 deg for titanium Grade 5.
Moved from titanium to EN24: lower twist, no spline shearing and lower cost.

Manufacturing and assembly

CNC machining, gear cutting, 3D printing, welding

Process
Mounts, sprockets and eccentric discs CNC machined; aluminium parts anodised.
Materials
Intermediate shaft EN19 and stubs EN24, both hardened. Halfshaft splines cut on a gear cutting machine. 3D printing was also used in the build.
Assembly
Mounts welded to the chassis, then chain alignment and tension checked.
Complete drivetrain built, fitted and raced on the finished car.

Weight and inertia comparison

ANSYS Workbench, Static Structural

Setup
Single vs dual chain drive modelled in CAD with real materials.
Finding
Dual chain drive is 11.59% heavier but has 54.4% lower moment of inertia.
Lower inertia gives faster response from the motor.

Motorshaft assembly

ANSYS Workbench, Static Structural

Setup
Torque on bolt holes with FOS 1.2 on the 140 Nm peak, chain load 6,000 N for bending, bearing load 6,579.8 N on the mount.
Max von Mises stress
Flange 114.9 MPa (torsion), 140.45 MPa (bending). Connector 54.35 MPa. 11T sprocket 374.07 MPa. Shaft bending 34.98 MPa. Mount 254.71 MPa.
All parts checked against loads before release to the vendor.

Intermediate shaft assembly

ANSYS Workbench, Static Structural

Setup
Torsion with 336 Nm on the splines, bending from chain forces at 15.8 deg and 92.8 deg chain angles. Bearing loads on discs and mounts.
Max von Mises stress
Shaft 322.27 MPa (torsion), 172.02 MPa (bending). Eccentric disc 61.26 MPa. Left mount 272.05 MPa. Right mount 177 MPa.
Shaft redesigned as one piece after the bolted coupling failed in testing.

Differential assembly and stubs

ANSYS Workbench, Static Structural

Setup
Bearing loads of 13,978 N (left) and 2,058.6 N (right) on the differential mounts. 977.45 Nm on 18 engaged teeth of the driven sprocket. 407.26 Nm on the stub splines.
Max von Mises stress
Left mount 335.27 MPa. Right mount 204.46 MPa. Driven sprocket 211.92 MPa. Left stub 357.76 MPa. Right stub 333.5 MPa.
Stub stresses led to the hardened EN24 design.

Testing

Static and dynamic tests on the drivetrain, and what each failure changed in the design.

Static testing of the new assembly

Static testing, EDS, failure analysis

Goal
Check alignment and tension of both chain drives on the welded chassis.
Method
Three days of static tests, after first testing the old assembly on the old chassis.
DateResult of static testing
22/08/24Chain misaligned on the driving sprocket and noisy. Motor mount position changed to fix it.
23/08/24Ran to 4,100 rpm with 40 Nm braking load. Chain alignment now good. Stopped by a cooling problem.
24/08/24At 76 Nm braking torque the three bolts in the two-piece intermediate shaft sheared. Motor then overspeeded to 6,500 rpm and the controller shut down.
Issues found and fixed within three days.

Failure: two-piece intermediate shaft

Static testing, EDS, failure analysis

What failed
Three bolts coupling the two shaft halves sheared.
Root cause
The shear load limit of the bolts was never checked.
Fix
Redesigned as one single-piece EN19 shaft, then retested.
Lesson: verify bolt shear capacity, not just part stress.

Material check on a fractured stub (EDS)

Dynamic testing, EDS, failure analysis

Goal
Find out if the vendor's Al 7075 stub was the wrong material after it broke on launch.
Method
Energy dispersive spectroscopy on the fracture, compared with Al 7075-T6 composition.
Outcome
Composition matched 7075-T6 (Al 87.07%, Zn 6.42%, Mg 3.15%), so the flaw was in the design.
Design changed to hardened EN24 steel stubs.
